newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU beef proposal may mean deferred oilseed payment.
newsitem.headline: EU beef proposal may mean deferred oilseed payment.

text.p: A proposal by the Irish EU Presidency to increase aid to farmers hit by the so-called mad cow crisis may entail deferring aid payments to oilseed producers.

The Irish Presidency proposed on Wednesday, the third day of a European Union farm ministers' meeting, an extra 500 milllion Ecus aid to break a deadlock over help for beef producers affected by the beef crisis.
To free more money for the livestock sector it suggested that 60 percent of an estimated 1.3 billion Ecus aid due to oilseed farmers in 1997 be postponed until 1998.

"The (Farm) Council considers that the continuing serious difficulties justify additional measures (including promotion) for the beef sector amounting to not less than 500 Mecus," Ireland said in its new compromise paper.
EU farm ministers had unanimously rejected an initial Irish compromise proposal on Tuesday, saying aid was insufficient and measures to cut beef surpluses were unacceptable.
French Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur, backed by Germany and other member states, warned that if extra aid was not provided there would be a fresh crisis among farmers.

But EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler has said that there was no more money available in the farm budget and emergency aid agreed by EU leaders in Florence in June, topped up by national payments, would cover estimated losses in 1996.
Losses following a 15 percent drop in EU beef demand are put at 1.2 billion Ecus in 1996.

The compromise text noted that 230 million Ecus of aid payable to beef producers in 1997 was brought forward to 1996 under an agreement drafted by EU farm ministers at an informal meeting in Killarney, Ireland, in September.
But bureaucratic problems meant that another 270 million Ecus was not paid out before the 1996 mid-October deadline.
An Irish official said farm ministers were discussing the new compromise but an early conclusion was unlikely.
